title: Microsoft Office suite: Word, Excel and PowerPoint

videos.script: Three programs, and the useful thing to know about each is not where the buttons are, because that moves. It is the model underneath, which has not moved in twenty years. {{model}} Word's model is that a document has structure, and formatting is what the structure looks like. A heading is a heading because it is marked as one, not because it is large and bold — and everything Word does well, from a table of contents to renumbering a hundred figures, falls out of that one distinction. {{word}} Excel's model is that a cell holds a value and a formula is a value computed from other cells. The trouble people have with Excel is almost never arithmetic. It is that Excel decides what type a thing is the moment you type it, silently, and it is sometimes wrong. {{excel}} PowerPoint's model is that a slide is a layout filled in, and the layout lives somewhere else entirely. {{ppt}} Three models, three sections, and every button in all three can move without any of it changing.
